attempts.summary: Configured a DHCP relay on node1 (the SONiC switch sitting between node2's and node3's segments) so node3 obtains its address from node2's isc-dhcp-server. Static /24 links were addressed: node1 eth1<->node2 enp8s0 on 192.168.50.0/24, node1 eth2<->node3 enp8s0 on 192.168.60.0/24. isc-dhcp-server was installed on node2 with a subnet declaration for 192.168.60.0/24 (pool 192.168.60.100-200) served via relay, plus a route back to that subnet through node1. dhcrelay was extracted from SONiC's dormant dhcp_relay docker feature and run persistently as a host systemd service on node1 (-id eth2 -iu eth1 192.168.50.2), with IP forwarding enabled. Verified end-to-end via tcpdump and dhcpd logs that DISCOVER/REQUEST/OFFER/ACK correctly relay across the segments, and node3 obtained lease 192.168.60.100 from node2's server. All three nodes (node2, node1, node3, in that order) were then restarted one at a time via native reboot; boot IDs changed on each, and post-restart verification confirmed all config (static addressing, routes, dhcrelay service, DHCP server, and the live DHCP-obtained address on node3) persisted and the relay path continued functioning after each restart.
